title: Coilback Desk Critter
summary: An original print-in-place fidget creature with four ball-jointed legs to pose and a helical spring tail to flick and bounce, printed fully assembled in one part.
coordinate_system: Origin at the center of the ground plane directly below the body's center, at bed height (Z=0). +X points toward the head/nose, +Y points to the creature's left, +Z points up.

parts.name: Coilback critter, print-in-place
parts.base_shape: Ellipsoid body with an integrated head, 4 ball-jointed legs, and a helical coil tail, printed as one part with clearance gaps at every joint
construction_steps: Create the body: a sphere of diameter 38 at (X=0, Y=0, Z=20), scaled non-uniformly to 50 (X) x 38 (Y) x 34 (Z) — an ellipsoid
Create the head: a sphere of diameter 22 at (X=32, Y=0, Z=26), scaled to 22 (X) x 22 (Y) x 20 (Z); union with the body and fillet the seam 4
Create two eye bumps: hemispheres, 6 diameter, at (X=36, Y=7, Z=28) and (X=36, Y=-7, Z=28); union with the head
For each of the 4 hip positions — (15,13,10), (15,-13,10), (-15,13,10), (-15,-13,10) — cut a spherical socket 9.6 diameter, 5 deep, into the body surface at that point

For each hip position, model a leg: a ball 9 diameter centered in its socket (0.3 clearance from the socket wall on all sides), connected by a neck cylinder 3 diameter x 2 long to a leg cylinder 5 diameter x 14 long, angled 20 degrees outward and downward from the hip toward the ground, ending in a foot hemisphere 6 diameter resting at Z=0

Model the tail: sweep a circle 4 diameter along a helix — axis along -X starting at (X=-25, Y=0, Z=20), helix radius 8 (tube center to axis), pitch 4.4, 8 turns, running from X=-25 to X=-60 — leaving a 0.4 gap between adjacent coil turns
Cap the tail's free end with a sphere 4 diameter

Union the body, head, eyes, and tail into one continuous shell; leave the leg balls and their sockets as separate mating surfaces with the clearance gap from step 5 intact so they rotate after printing
parts.print_orientation: Standing on its 4 feet, tail lying back along the bed

assembly_steps: None — prints ready to use. The leg joints rotate and the tail flexes as soon as the print is removed from the bed
